terms.gloss: the science of machines and devices; technology
terms.comment: Gellius’s phrase for the art by which Archytas made a wooden dove fly; Morgan–Owens gives it for technology. Mēchanicus is ante-classical and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short).

terms.latin: artēs mēchanicae, artium mēchanicārum f. pl.
terms.comment: Morgan–Owens also allows artēs māchinālēs or fabrīlēs.

phrases.latin: simulācrum columbae ē lignō ab Archȳtā ratiōne quādam disciplīnāque mēchanicā factum volāsse
phrases.english: that a model of a dove made of wood by Archytas, by a certain method and mechanical skill, flew

sources: Lewis & Short: mechanicus · Lewis & Short: disciplina · Lewis & Short: ars · Lewis & Short: technicus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. technology.
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-gellius), checked against the editions named there.
Traupman has no word for technology; he gives māchinālis scientia for engineering (pp. 166, 310).
